instruction.text: Sort the methods of travelling to school.

trainers.hint: Methods of public transport, such as trains and buses, are considered to be sustainable as they use less fuel than if the people were in individual cars.

feedback.finish: When going to school, it’s more sustainable to use public transport, to cycle or to walk. This reduces the amount of harmful gas emissions you produce.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: One of the most common types of waste is clothing waste, especially school uniforms, which children grow out of very quickly.

atoms.a: What do you think you could do with your old uniforms to be more sustainable?
b: put them in your wardrobe and forget about them

feedback.finish: Maybe you could buy your next uniform second-hand from someone else?

atoms.b: Learning and ((++raising ignoring)) awareness about sustainability in school is very important.
There are lots of ways you can make your school and classroom more ((++sustainable damaging)).

instruction.text: Select the recycling bins to learn how you can make your classroom more sustainable.

feedback.finish: Most schools have different recycling bins in the classroom, where pupils and teachers can dispose of their recyclable waste responsibly.

atoms.b: A fun school project, and a creative way to use plastic ((++waste haste)), is to make ecobricks.
An ecobrick is a plastic bottle tightly packed with small bits of ((food ++plastic)) until it’s completely full and solid.
Ecobricks help to ((++minimise maximise)) the amount of loose plastic that ends up in oceans and landfills.

instruction.text: Match the steps of making an ecobrick to the images.

atoms.b: Wash and dry the bottle and plastic waste.
Cut the plastic waste into small pieces.
Tightly pack the bottle with the plastic waste.

instruction.text: Drag the plastic waste to the bottle to complete your ecobrick.

text: Ecobricks can then be repurposed for a variety of things, such as for building materials and other creative projects.
